To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sensorial and the physicochemical characteristics (pH, expressible water, fat release, adhesiveness, elasticity, firmness, brightness, colour intensity and smoke odour, TMA, TBARS, TMA, amine odor) of salmon (Salmo silar) fillets are affected by the type of smoke treatment (liquid smoke flavorings and cold-smoke wood smoke).
“The smoking processes studied have a significant effect on the sensorial characteristics, physicochemical properties and shelf life of salmon fillets”.
the smoke treatments used in this study had a significant effect on the physicochemical and sensorial characteristics of Atlantic salmon fillets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of different smoking processes and their effect on the quality of Atlantic salmon fillets during storage.
a comparison of the effects of four smoking processes on the physicochemical characteristics and sensory quality of salmon fillets.
identifying the effects of four smoking processes on the physicochemical and sensory properties of smoked salmon fillets, as well as the effect of the storage time on these characteristics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

smoke flavouring FA has the lowest effect on the physicochemical properties and sensorial characteristics of smoked salmon, whereas smoke generated with BS or OS has the greatest impact on such characteristics.
smoke flavouring FB and BS or OS wood smoke are suitable for smoking salmon, but smoke flavouring FA is not.
the use of smoke flavouring FA is not recommended, while smoke flavouring FB is a good alternative, especially for those consumers who do not like the typical smoked odour.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
smoking with liquid smoke flavouring FA or wood smoke (OS or BS) is an effective way to extend the shelf life of salmon fillets.

smoke flavouring FB is more effective in preserving salmon fillets than the smoke flavouring FA, while the smoke from wood is more effective in maintaining the characteristics of salmon fillets than smoke flavouring FB, but less so than smoke flavouring FA.
smoke flavouring FB has the best sensorial characteristics, followed by OS smoke and BS smoke, and finally, the control samples (Cn).
The main takeaway from our work is that
smoking is a very useful tool for improving the sensorial and functional properties of fish products, especially if it is performed with smoke flavourings.

smoking processes have a significant influence on the sensorial characteristics of smoked fish products, and that the type of smoking process has a greater influence on the sensorical and physicochemical quality of the product than the storage time.

smoke flavouring FB, BS and OS are suitable for the cold-smoking treatment of Atlantic salmon fillets, and that the use of smoke flavouring FA is not recommended for the smoking of Atlantic salmon fillet.
